roadmap.scope: Slice 1 (phase 01): pure claim_domain::authority person rules and a CLI gate entry from local checks (U-OOS-3), gating claim add and the shared sign batch for github:<login> subjects; dispute and withdrawal stay open. Slice 2 (phase 02): v8 repo_authority_checks, read_repo_authority with its recorded-fixture contract test (U-OOS-8), authority verify, a behaviour-neutral sign_permitted refactor, behaviour-neutral shipped-suite migrations, then repo subjects gated in claim add, scrape --sign and claim publish. Slice 3 (phase 03): score_attested, labels, --include-unattested, viewer and search. Slice 4 (phase 04): the review-app share draft only (SA-1). Slice 5 (phase 05): imported candidates kept locally and listed offline.

conventions.paradigm: ADR-007 functional Rust. kind, requirement, classify, the CLI gate entry, hand-off data, labels and score_attested are pure (claim-domain, scoring, scraper-domain, viewer-domain, review-domain). Verbs, the viewer and adapters do I/O only. ADTs over flags (Kind, Requirement, Authority, Unattested reason, PermitBasis, SigningRefusal). No enum arm or function exists only for tests: each lands in the step whose production code first constructs or calls it (ruling M4). ONE explicit exception (ruling F6): GithubPort::read_repo_authority is called only by its contract test in 02-02 and gains its production caller, the authority verify verb, in the very next step 02-03. Crafter: nw-functional-software-crafter.
conventions.test_paradigm: Acceptance: example-based subprocess runs of the REAL openlore binary over the real DuckDB store, fakes only for GitHub, PDSes and the network index (DISTILL walking-skeleton strategy). Pure core: proptest (256 cases) against the CORE-OOS oracles plus crafter-owned proptests in claim-domain / scoring with state-delta (tests/common/state_delta.rs) over a declared universe; single-example unit tests only with a `// bypass:` reason. Adapters: real DuckDB and recorded GitHub fixtures, never mocked. CLI and HTTP scenarios stay single-example (wiring, not invariants).
conventions.scenario_fns: `<test target>::<fn>`. CLI targets (crates/cli): owner_only_signing (slice 1), owner_only_signing_repos (slices 2 and 5), owner_only_signing_readers (slice 3), owner_only_signing_core (CORE-OOS properties). Review app target (crates/openlore-review-app): owner_only_signing_review_app (SA-1). Target names stay stable (ruling L4). Each step lists every fn it activates, RED driver first. Every #[ignore] fn of the five targets maps to exactly one step; the ACTIVE guards PS-3, PS-7 and IC-5 are named in the steps whose code they protect. regenerate_the_frozen_v7_store_fixture is a fixture regenerator, not a step, and stays ignored. Steps with no DISTILL activation (02-02 contract test, 02-05 refactor, 02-06 migrations) name their test_file / scenario_name as the test that guards them and leave scenario_fns empty.
conventions.rider_classes: Each step names one RED driver. Other activations are a secondary driver (new behaviour, RED on activation: un-ignore, see it RED, make it green within the step) or a guard (expected green on activation or already active: record a mutation RED per mutation_red_on_pass).
conventions.core_binding_red: A step binding a CORE-OOS property first lands the production function as a signature stub with a todo!() body, then points the sut_* binding at it, so un-ignoring gives a panic RED, never a compile error (DWD-OOS-10). CORE-OOS-3 and CORE-OOS-4 generate repo rows, so they stay #[ignore] until the step that first constructs those values in production (ruling M4, named in F7): the classify tier Authority::Attested(RepoListed) / Attested(Owner) for repos is first constructed by the authority verify verb in 02-03 (CORE-OOS-3 activates there); PermitBasis::RepoListed is first constructed by the CLI entry may_sign_from_checks in the RA-10 step 02-07 (CORE-OOS-4 activates there). Person-tier rows are covered earlier by crafter-owned proptests in claim-domain. A property may move unchanged in name and assertions into crates/claim-domain/tests or crates/scoring/tests.
conventions.test_edit_allow_list: (1) Removing the #[ignore] of a named scenario fn. (2) Replacing a named sut_* todo!() body in owner_only_signing_core.rs with ONE real call plus view mapping. (3) U-OOS-12: one added row in PS-2 (01-03, ruling M6) and one in RA-4 (02-03), built only from existing support/authority.rs vocabulary. (4) Wording pins in support/authority.rs, one-line edits only (DWD-OOS-3). (5) Shipped-suite migration per conventions.shipped_suite_migration and each step's shipped_migrations. (6) U-OOS-9 request-log exclusion in crates/test-support/src/fake_github_accounts.rs. Forbidden otherwise: assertions, oracles, strategies, universe slots, guardrails and test names of the owner_only_signing* targets. A missing vocabulary step stops the step and goes to nw-acceptance-designer. Crafter-owned tests in their own crates (adapter-duckdb, adapter-github contract tests, claim-domain, scoring, cli unit tests, review-app unit tests, xtask synthetic violations) may be added.
conventions.shipped_suite_migration: DISTILL wave-decisions lists the shipped acceptance files the behaviour change breaks. Each is listed in files_to_modify AND in shipped_migrations (file -> allowed change) of the step that migrates it, so every step ends with the whole cli and review-app suites green. Repo-subject Givens migrate in the behaviour-neutral step 02-06, BEFORE the repo gate turns on in 02-07 (ruling F4). Change types: SEEDED-GIVEN (a Given seeded with authority through support/authority.rs steps, e.g. the_repo_holds_authority_file + given_jeff_verified_authority_of, or a seeded link), NON-GITHUB-SUBJECT (only where the test does not depend on the github: scheme), HELPER-ABSORBED (the shared seeding helper is migrated, the caller file needs no edit unless its own Given signs directly), EXPECTATION (only the DISTILL-named flips: score expectations, IR-16b, CORE-6 re-point, a refused cross-person signature), ONLY-IF-CHANGED (edited only if its outcome actually changes). RED protocol: at RED the crafter runs the full `cargo nextest run -p cli` (and `-p openlore-review-app` where the step touches it), records the failing set in the execution log, and lists every failing shipped file not yet in the step's shipped_migrations there (with its change type) before the step ends; no allowed change fits = the step stops.
conventions.transitional_risks: Orchestrator rulings (accepted: the work stays on the oos-deliver branch until every step is done). T1: Required(Repo) assertions are not gated in phase 01 (no observation store before 02-01). From 02-05 every sign goes through sign_permitted; repo-subject permits come from the named transitional entry permit_ungated_repo_t1 (basis PermitBasis::UngatedT1) inside claim_domain::authority. T1 callers per step (ruling L5): 01-01..02-04 none (repo subjects sign through the old inline path); 02-05 claim_add and sign_batch; 02-06 claim_add and sign_batch (unchanged; migrations only); 02-07 sign_batch only (claim add switches to may_sign_from_checks); 02-08 sign_batch only; 02-09 none: entry, arm and its xtask rule are deleted, T1 closed. claim_counter, claim_retract and identity_link NEVER call it: they mint exempt permits from 02-05 (ruling F1). Enforced by xtask t1_entry_only_from_sign_batch (02-05..02-08). T2: unpublished person-subject claims stay publishable without a permit until 02-11 (claim publish gate), closed by the crafter-owned RED test named there (ruling F3).
conventions.gate_order: Every way to mint the shared SigningPermit, all inside claim_domain::authority (ruling F2): (1) may_sign — ADR-089, shipped before this feature, same-request reads, basis PermitBasis::Owner, kept byte-for-byte, the only entry the review app calls, never deleted. (2) may_sign_from_checks (crafter may rename) — introduced 01-01 (person, basis PermitBasis::Owner), 7-day window 01-04, basis PermitBasis::RepoListed first constructed 02-07; kept. (3) exempt_permit (crafter may rename) — introduced 02-05 with the NEW arm PermitBasis::Exempt, first constructed there for counters, retractions, identity links and non-github: subjects; later used by claim publish to re-publish an already-published claim (02-11); kept. (4) permit_ungated_repo_t1 — introduced 02-05 with the NEW arm PermitBasis::UngatedT1, deleted with that arm in 02-09. sign_permitted (02-05) and publish_signed_claim(&SigningPermit) (02-11) consume permits; neither mints one.
conventions.sign_sites: Six IdentityPort::sign call sites: claim_add, claim_counter, claim_retract, sign_batch, philosophy_add, identity_link. Five route through sign_permitted in 02-05; claim_counter, claim_retract and identity_link use exempt_permit; claim_add and sign_batch use may_sign_from_checks (person), exempt_permit (exempt) or the T1 entry (repo); philosophy_add (philosophy records, not claims) is the only allowlisted site. Six publish_signed_claim callers: claim_publish, claim_add, claim_counter, claim_retract, sign_batch, identity_link, all changed in 02-11.
conventions.migrations: v8 = repo_authority_checks only, in 02-01 (forward-only, idempotent, insert-only, live probe). imported_candidates is v9 in 05-01: v8 can reach users' stores before slice 5 and stores are forward-only (DESIGN and DISTILL wrote 'v8 imported_candidates'; RA-12/RA-12b guardrails count only v7 and v8). Never regenerate the frozen v7 fixture after 02-01.
conventions.arch_rules_note: Each step's arch_rules field names the xtask rules it adds, amends or deletes, plus structural checks moved out of criteria (ruling L2); each rule ships a synthetic-violation test in xtask and must keep `cargo xtask check-arch` green on the real tree. Criteria state user-visible or unit-property outcomes only (ruling L3).
conventions.test_runs: Feature targets: `cargo nextest run -p cli --test owner_only_signing --test owner_only_signing_repos --test owner_only_signing_readers --test owner_only_signing_core` and `cargo nextest run -p openlore-review-app --test owner_only_signing_review_app`. Every step's green list ends with cargo test for each touched crate, `cargo test -p xtask`, `cargo xtask check-arch`, `cargo nextest run -p cli` and `cargo nextest run -p openlore-review-app` (ruling H1). Scoped crates only, never the workspace.
conventions.done_per_step: A step is done when its scenario fns are un-ignored and green, the active guards (PS-3, PS-7, IC-5) pass, every arch_rules entry holds, and every command in its green list passes.
conventions.mutation_red_on_pass: A guard green on activation gets a recorded mutation RED: break the named rule in production code, run the guard and show it fails, revert. Rule, failing scenario and revert go in the commit message and the execution log RED phase.
conventions.wording: Labels, refusal fragments, hand-off lines, footers and usage messages are DISTILL pins in tests/acceptance/support/authority.rs (DWD-OOS-3); DELIVER may change a pin only by a one-line edit there.
conventions.exit_codes: A refused signature exits non-zero; candidates are still listed (DWD-OOS-4). Usage mistakes exit 2 (RD-11).
conventions.forge_build_time: Forge 6 (DISTILL R6): 01-01 measures the acceptance build of the five new targets once and records it in the execution log and step notes. No consolidation of owner_only_signing_core in this roadmap (ruling L4); an over-budget result is reported to the orchestrator.
conventions.deferred_rulings: H5 / U-OOS-10: the refusal tally is NOT built (a counter with no production caller is dead code). Deferred: the CLI has no telemetry channel; the review app's existing publish.refused.* counters cover the review app.
conventions.upstream_ids: U-OOS-2 -> 02-06 (WS-1..WS-10 migrated before the gate). U-OOS-3 -> 01-01, 01-04, 02-07. U-OOS-8 -> 02-02 (before any repo signing step). U-OOS-9 -> 02-09 and 04-01. U-OOS-10 -> deferred (deferred_rulings). U-OOS-12 -> 01-03 (PS-2 row) and 02-03 (RA-4 --mine row).
